previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal and gastrostomy tube in place) was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain with nausea/vomiting and diarrhea. Initial evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs; CT abdomen/pelvis and right upper quadrant ultrasound found no acute intraabdominal process, no biliary obstruction, and an appropriately positioned G-tube, with ultrasound noting fatty liver. Diarrhea resolved early and symptoms evolved into constipation, with abdominal radiograph showing mild fecal loading and no obstruction; stool cultures were negative and C. difficile testing was cancelled due to formed stool. Pain management emphasized non-opioid strategies given ulcer/NSAID intolerance and opioid-associated constipation, including scheduled acetaminophen, gradual uptitration of gabapentin, bowel regimen (senna/docusate with PRN polyethylene glycol and bisacodyl), and PRN simethicone for gas, while continuing home acid suppression and chronic medications. She tolerated a regular diet, ambulated independently, and was discharged home without opioids with outpatient chronic pain follow-up and return precautions.
